extendedContent.title: Origins & Mythology
extendedContent.content: The Comb of the Fairy originates from Korean oral tradition, appearing in numerous folktales and myths centered around interactions between humans and celestial beings. These stories often involve a mortal stumbling upon a group of fairies bathing in a secluded location, typically a hidden pond or waterfall. The fairies' garments and accessories, including the magical comb, are left unguarded. The mortal might steal the comb, hoping to use its power or force a fairy to marry him. Other tales portray the comb as a gift bestowed upon a virtuous mortal, granting them blessings or protecting them from harm. The mythology surrounding the comb reinforces the idea of fairies as both alluring and dangerous figures, capable of great kindness but also easily angered or deceived. The specific powers and attributes of the comb vary depending on the region and the storyteller, reflecting the diverse and evolving nature of Korean folklore.

extendedContent.title: Role & Significance
extendedContent.content: The Comb of the Fairy plays a significant role in Korean culture as a symbol of beauty, fortune, and the delicate balance between the human and spirit realms. It represents the feminine ideal, often associated with purity, grace, and ethereal charm. The comb's presence in folktales serves as a reminder of the potential rewards and perils of interacting with the supernatural. It highlights the importance of respecting the natural world and maintaining harmony with the spirit world. The stories also often carry moral lessons, cautioning against greed, deceit, and the abuse of power. The comb, therefore, functions as a cultural artifact, embodying both aesthetic ideals and ethical values. Its presence in stories also helped explain natural phenomenon to those without scientific knowledge.

extendedContent.title: Symbolism & Interpretation
extendedContent.content: The Comb of the Fairy is rich in symbolic meaning. It represents not only physical beauty but also inner virtue and spiritual purity. The act of combing one's hair is itself symbolic of self-care, refinement, and the ordering of one's life. The comb, therefore, becomes a tool for achieving both external and internal harmony. The fairy association further enhances its symbolic power, linking it to the realm of the supernatural and the potential for magical transformation. The comb can also be interpreted as a symbol of female empowerment, representing the ability to influence one's own destiny through beauty, wisdom, and connection to the spirit world. The loss of the comb can symbolize loss of virtue or fortune.

extendedContent.title: Legacy & Influence
extendedContent.content: The Comb of the Fairy continues to resonate in modern Korean culture, appearing in contemporary literature, film, and television. It serves as a nostalgic reminder of traditional folklore and a source of inspiration for artistic expression. The image of the fairy with her magical comb evokes a sense of wonder and enchantment, appealing to audiences of all ages. The comb also appears in modern beauty and cosmetics advertising, leveraging its association with beauty and magical transformation. The enduring popularity of the Comb of the Fairy demonstrates the lasting power of Korean folklore and its ability to adapt to contemporary contexts, continuing to shape the cultural imagination. It is also used as a symbol of Korean identity in some contexts.

description: The Comb of the Fairy is a recurring motif in Korean folktales and legends, representing the ethereal beauty and power associated with fairies (Seonnyeo). These combs are not mere hair accessories; they are often imbued with magic, capable of bestowing beauty, granting wishes, or even controlling the weather. Stories involving the Comb of the Fairy frequently center on mortals who encounter these celestial beings and, through either cunning or kindness, gain access to the comb's power. The loss or theft of the comb is a common plot device, symbolizing the disruption of the natural order or the consequences of greed. The comb serves as a tangible link between the human and fairy realms, highlighting the allure and potential dangers of interacting with the supernatural. Its presence in folklore reinforces the idea of fairies as powerful, yet vulnerable, figures in the Korean cultural imagination. The attributes and function of the comb varies based on the region and specific folktale being told, but it is generally associated with feminine beauty, blessings, and the connection to the spirit realm.
